subject: SparkPlug accelerator: promo aggregation & tiered credits
messages:

Cc: SparkPlug Labs Finance <finance@sparkplug.ai>

Subject: SparkPlug accelerator - promo credits & bulk billing for cohort

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — SparkPlug is excited about the latency and predictable cost profile you showed. We're preparing the cohort onboarding plan and have two asks we want to align on before we finalize the SOW:

1) Aggregation of promotional credits: we run two cohorts this fall and would like the onboarding promo credits to be pooled under the same account so we can shift credits between teams as needed. Is that supported?

2) Tiered credits & billing cadence: our finance team prefers a monthly consolidated invoice rather than per-cohort invoices. If we commit to a 12-month reserved pool post-pilot, could we get a tiered discount on top of the promo credits (example: 10% off committed usage after credits are consumed)?

I've attached a simple usage estimate (cohort_credit_usage_estimate.xlsx) and the term sheet we usually use (SparkPlug_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf) for context. Can you outline what carveouts we'd need for credit aggregation and whether an invoice consolidation option exists?

Quick answers will help our procurement kick off.

Best,
Alex
Head of Partnerships
SparkPlug Labs
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@sparkplug.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkPlug accelerator - promo credits & bulk billing for cohort

Alex — thanks for the context and the attachments. Short answers up front:

- Credit pooling: yes, we can route promo credits to a single billing identity and allow internal reallocation between cohorts; there are accounting flags we set on our side so credits show as "program" rather than per-project.

- Billing cadence: monthly consolidated invoicing is possible for customers on a committed billing flow. To surface a tiered discount tied to committed spend we'll need a committed capacity addendum (reserved pool) in the contract.

I'll loop in Ben and Marissa for the concession/pricing details and ask them to propose 2 options (minimal admin + low discount; committed pool + higher discount). Can you confirm who signs on your side (legal or finance) and whether you have a procurement template?

Kimberly Park
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@sparkplug.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkPlug accelerator - promo credits & bulk billing for cohort

Alex / Kim — following up with two concrete packaging options based on your ask and the estimate you shared. We modeled using the attached workbook and these are back-of-envelope numbers; legal will need the final redlines.

Option A — Flexible pooling (low friction)
- Promo credits pooled to a single billing identity, transferable between cohorts by SparkPlug admin.
- No committed spend required.
- Billing: monthly consolidated invoice.
- Discount: no committed discount; we can offer a one-time 20% uplift in onboarding credits for the first cohort as a gesture (non-recurring).
- Notes: Minimal contract change; we issue a one-line amendment and update billing flags.

Option B — Committed pool (higher savings)
- Reserved 12-month committed capacity (prepaid or committed spend).
- Promo credits pooled and applied first; once exhausted, committed capacity pricing applies.
- Billing: monthly consolidated invoice with committed discount applied to consumption beyond credits.
- Discount: tiered discount schedule — 5% at $50k+/mo, 10% at $100k+/mo (post-credit).
- Notes: Requires an addendum for committed capacity and an agreed forecast runway; 30-day notice to scale commitments.

Attachments: I put the detail in "cohort_credit_usage_estimate.xlsx" (tab: pricing_scenarios).

Questions for SparkPlug:
- Would you prefer prepaid committed pool or pay-as-you-go with a revenue commitment?
- Who will sign the addendum on your side?

If helpful, Marissa can prepare a short amendment draft for Option B to speed legal review.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Growth, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Li <alex@sparkplug.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: SparkPlug Labs Finance <finance@sparkplug.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkPlug accelerator - promo credits & bulk billing for cohort

Ben / Kimberly — thanks, that framing is helpful. We prefer Option B (committed pool) but we will need to present both alternatives to finance. A few clarifications:

- We prefer pay-as-you-go with a revenue commitment rather than full prepayment. Can Option B support that?
- The discount thresholds you proposed look good; can you add a guaranteed predictability clause (e.g., if usage drops below forecast for two consecutive months, we get a one-time credit top-up or runway extension)?
- Signature: procurement signs financial amendments; legal prefers our standard addendum template (attached). Who should I put as the Redwood counterparty on the addendum?

If you can draft the short addendum for Option B (pay-as-you-go + commit) and add a clause around shortfall protection, we can circulate to finance/legal tomorrow.

Thanks,
Alex
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@sparkplug.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SparkPlug accelerator - promo credits & bulk billing for cohort

Alex — great, Option B (pay-as-you-go with commit) is doable. Marissa will draft the addendum that matches:

- Reserved 12-month committed pool; billed monthly on actual consumption (no prepayment).
- Promo credits apply first; committed discount schedule applies to post-credit consumption (5%/10% thresholds as Ben noted).
- Shortfall protection: 1x runway credit equal to 10% of the monthly committed amount if usage < 60% of forecast for two consecutive months; applies once during the 12-month term.

Next steps (internal assignments):
- Marissa Cole: draft addendum and highlight the rights/limitations of credit pooling; include a clean redline for SparkPlug's template. (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Priyom Das: confirm billing flags and whether we can show pooled credits as a single line item on the invoice; prepare a sample monthly invoice. (ETA: 48 hours)
- Ben: confirm final discount table and approval threshold for one-time onboarding uplift.

Alex — we'll target a draft by Tue morning so you can run it past procurement. Kimberly will be the Redwood counterparty on the addendum (Kimberly Park, Redwood Inference).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
